scope: Independent review of Measured's diagnostic serialization and regression test, workflow purpose/dose gates and tests, diagnostic contract, and freeze/supervisor/launcher scripts. Excludes src/wan.rs and tests/wan_persistent.rs authored by this reviewer; independent production/CLI review is separate.
conclusions: Measured copies the transport failure only after its existing timers finish, when the operation failed and the HTTP request counter advanced. Local no-exchange failures and successful operations serialize null instead of reusing stale diagnostics. Existing CPU, wall and body accounting is unchanged.
The retained HTTP429 regression checks the exact five sanitized fields and excludes token, URL, header and body sentinels. This review does not self-approve the underlying transport sanitizer.

The workflow validates diagnostic versus pilot purpose and derives a fixed shard list. Diagnostic mode executes only shard 0, at most six sessions and 66 transfers, with first-attempt/source gates and no transfer retry. Generating all six deterministic plan files does not execute the other shards.

The launcher explicitly sets diagnostic purpose, pins the frozen source and actual receiver digest, validates the single HTTPS relay URL and rejected preflight, and uses a fresh registration. The secret is supplied through stdin to gh secret and the transfer-step environment; it is not emitted in receipts or shell tracing.

The supervisor uses dedicated task paths, a 4 GiB free-space floor, exclusive evidence-directory creation, and a bounded receiver lifetime. Its cleanup trap sends signals only to recorded children still parented by that supervisor, then waits. It does not remove the failed campaign's cache or evidence.

The diagnostic retains the 500 ms policy, existing workload and failure behavior. Always-run checksum/artifact steps retain partial failures. A completed diagnostic would not qualify as a replacement performance campaign or establish a timeout cause by itself.
release_limit: One newly registered diagnostic, at most 66 transfers, after the separate independent transport/CLI approval. Preserve the original incomplete run and all new outcomes. No performance, WAN acceptance, timeout-causation, or production security certification claim.
